messages.m1: Usability issues in the new-user flow have been piling up for two weeks, and I got seven more user reports last night. If we do not fix this, people will simply vote with their feet 😵‍💫
messages.m2: A heads-up: if we do not tackle tech debt this week, development speed will keep dropping next release. It is already charging us interest.
messages.m3: We only have enough resources to commit to one direction. {role}, you have just joined the discussion—help us pick a direction?

choices.a: I suggest fixing the new-user flow first. Users clearly feel the pain; let us restore the core experience this week.
choices.b: Ship the monetization feature first, but define success metrics and a stop-loss line together—we own the revenue outcome.
choices.c: Pay down tech debt this week; otherwise every future iteration gets slower. I will make the long-term payoff clear.

messages.m1: Customers are reporting that payments are stuck, and tickets keep coming in. About 8% of users are affected now.
messages.m2: We have traced it to a dependent service, and recovery should take about 30 minutes. I need someone to shield me from external communication.
messages.m3: {role}, are you there? Someone needs to align the public statement, support messaging, and fix cadence. Can you decide how we proceed?

choices.a: Share the impact scope and estimated recovery time first, align support and public messaging, and I will update every 15 minutes.
choices.b: Engineering focuses fully on the fix, and everyone else holds off on external messaging. I will run the postmortem and explain once we recover.
choices.c: Start a 15-minute war room now: engineering fixes, support reassures, PR prepares the statement—I will keep the pace.

messages.m1: This onboarding animation is not decoration—it helps first-time users understand the spatial relationships. Remove it and the experience feels jarring.
messages.m2: A full implementation takes at least two extra weeks, and I am not confident about low-end device performance. With the current schedule, we will definitely slip.
messages.m3: We seem stuck. {role}, can you propose a path that everyone can move forward with?

choices.a: Keep the full experience first. It solves the new-user comprehension problem; let us renegotiate the schedule instead of sacrificing core value.
choices.b: Ship a lightweight version on time, validate it with real data, then decide whether to invest in the full interaction.
choices.c: Keep the key onboarding moments and simplify the rest; let us build a prototype today and test it with users tomorrow.

messages.m1: Quick heads-up: the CEO has moved his next meeting earlier, so our review is cut from 30 minutes to 15.
messages.m2: I have updated the budget figures in the document. I suggest skipping the page-by-page walkthrough—there really is not enough time.
messages.m3: {role}, I have 15 minutes. Tell me directly: what is most worth betting on next quarter, and why?

choices.a: I will spend 3 minutes on the conclusion, 7 on data and results, and the last 5 only on resources I need you to approve.
choices.b: I will start with one key user story, prove the opportunity with data, and end with actions for next quarter.
choices.c: I will give one long-term call: where the market is heading, why we can win, and the three things we must do now.

interview.fallbackQuestion: How do you understand the role of {role}?

feedback.fallback: You expressed your judgment clearly. Keep watching how the team responds—good decisions also need to be received well.
feedback.scene1: Your response spelled out the trade-off and the reasoning, which makes it easier for the team to act. Add a success criterion and your decision becomes even stronger.
feedback.scene2: You organized people and cadence first—in an incident that matters more than jumping in to fix code yourself. Keep updating; silence amplifies anxiety.
feedback.scene3: You did not rush to take sides; you pulled the debate back to users and validation. That is mature. Good collaboration is not each side giving ground—it is finding evidence together.
feedback.scene4: Daring to cover only the most important things in fifteen minutes is a high-level skill. Lead with the conclusion, the evidence, and the items that need a decision—it carries more weight.
